events.help: module specific options. See hydra -U <module> what options are available.
events.previous_help: minimum length of a valid password

events.help: ignore an existing restore file (dont wait 10 seconds)
use old SSL v2 and v3
specify the format for the -o FILE: text(default), json, jsonv1
disable use of symbols in -x bruteforce, see above
verbose mode / show login+pass combination for each attempt
events.previous_help: verbose mode / show login+pass combination for each attempt debug mode

events.help: restore a previously aborted session. Requires a hydra.restore file was written. Options are restored, but can be changed by setting them after -R on the command line
events.previous_help: restore a previously aborted session. Requires a hydra.restore file was written. No other options are allowed when using -R

events.help: the wait time in seconds per login attempt over all threads (-t 1 is recommended) This usually only makes sense if a low task number is used, .e.g -t 1
events.previous_help: the minimum number of sets required (default: all given)

events.help: ignore an existing restore file (don't wait 10 seconds)
events.previous_help: ignore an existing restore file (dont wait 10 seconds)

-C.help: colon separated "login:pass" format, instead of -L/-P options

-F.help: exit after the first found login/password pair for any host (for usage with -M)

-I.help: ignore an existing restore file (don't wait 10 seconds)

-M.help: server list for parallel attacks, one entry per line

-O.help: use old SSL v2 and v3

-R.help: restore a previously aborted session. Requires a hydra.restore file was written. Options are restored, but can be changed by setting them after -R on the command line

-W.help: defines a wait time between each connection a task performs. This usually only makes sense if a low task number is used, .e.g -t 1

-b.help: specify the format for the -o FILE: text(default), json, jsonv1

-c.help: the wait time in seconds per login attempt over all threads (-t 1 is recommended) This usually only makes sense if a low task number is used, .e.g -t 1

-e.help: additional checks, "n" for null password, "s" try login as pass, "r" try the reverse login as pass

-f.help: exit after the first found login/password pair (per host if -M)

-i.help: file to read passwords from (default: stdin)

-l.help: or -L FILE login with LOGIN name, or load several logins from FILE

-m.help: module specific options. See hydra -U <module> what options are available.

-o.help: write found login/password pairs to FILE instead of stdout

-p.help: or -P FILE try password PASS, or load several passwords from FILE

-s.help: if the service is on a different default port, define it here

-t.help: run TASKS number of connects in parallel (default: 16)

-u.help: by default Hydra checks all passwords for one login and then tries the next login. This option loops around the passwords, so the first password is tried on all logins, then the next password.

-v.help: verbose mode / show login+pass combination for each attempt

-w.help: defines the max wait time in seconds for responses (default: 32)

-x.help: generate passwords from min to max length. charset can contain 1 for numbers, a for lowcase and A for upcase characters. Any other character is added is put to the list. Example: 1:2:a1%. The generated passwords will be of length 1 to 2 and contain lowcase letters, numbers and/or percent signs and dots.

-y.help: disable use of symbols in -x bruteforce, see above
